text:
sam: Quick spike — we keep hitting sustained pressure on dedicated pools during batch windows. thinking about an automated fallback to a spot/ephemeral lane but want to minimize KV-cache churn and tail-latency blips. thoughts?
anika: +1 on spot fallback, but we need deterministic eviction order and a staged migration so cold KV entries don't explode latencies. random eviction = bad.
ben: Can we define a soft-drain flow: 1) mark tenant as in-fallback, 2) send new sessions to spot pool, 3) let existing in-flight finish on dedicated for TTL, 4) move background prewarm of KV to targets?
maria: Sounds sensible. also need accounting for burst credits — if a tenant has leftover burst budget they should be first-class for staying on dedicated. otherwise we punish customers who paid for reserved behavior.
sam: Right. Proposal sketch: eviction_score = alpha * (1 - sla_priority) + beta * (1 - burst_credit_ratio) + gamma * recent_error_rate. Lower score = protected. We then drain ascending score.
anika: Love that. we should also include locality factor: tenants with models pinned to GPUs or with large KV footprints should be higher protected since migration cost is heavy.
ben: Operationally, operator needs to expose a simple intent API, something like: 
```
PATCH /pools/:id/fallback
{ "threshold": 0.82, "mode": "staged", "max_migrations": 3 }
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback hook exists for pool-fallback if tail-90p latency > 200ms for 2min. :white_check_mark:
maria: We must avoid oscillation. If we shift too aggressively to spot and then traffic recovers, we shouldn't re-migrate everything back immediately. hysteresis window + cooldown per-tenant.
sam: Suggested cooldown: per-tenant cooldown = max(30m, 2 * migration_time_estimate). Also a global cooldown where we only allow N migrations per minute to avoid operator thrashing.
anika: For KV migration, propose a cheap warming phase: copy prefixes asynchronously to spot nodes while still serving from dedicated. once warm fraction > 60% we start routing a small percentage of new requests (canary). scale canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% with success checks.
ben: Would like a config snippet to be concrete: 
```
fallback_policy:
  mode: staged
  threshold_qps_util: 0.85
  eviction_policy: sla_locality_burst
  warm_threshold: 0.6
  canary_steps: [0.05, 0.2, 1.0]
  max_concurrent_migrations: 2
  tenant_cooldown_m: 60
```
maria: Also: billing window amortization for burst credits. If tenant used burst in last billing window but still has negative balance we should proportionally reduce eviction weight instead of an absolute block.
sam: Good point. include 'billing_decay' param to weight older credits less.
anika: Edge case: what about long-lived KV sessions that are stateful (like chat with big prefix cache)? migrating those will always be expensive. we should allow opt-out or pinning flag on tenant config: "pin_on_dedicated: true" which makes them immune unless we're in emergency mode.
ben: Emergency mode = only when pool freeable_capacity < X% and predicted unmet_sla risk > Y. emergency should have its own escalation log + oncall pager.
ops-bot: incident-bot: created fallback-emergency runbook link: https://wiki/redd/evict-fallback-runbook — include steps to revert.
maria: Monitoring/observability needs: leaderboard of migration cost, migration success rate, canary failure reasons, KV warm fraction metric. We'll surface these in Console per-pool.
sam: One more op-sanity: tie fallback decision to model-compatibility matrix. if spot nodes have quantized model variant, we need translation policy. prefer identical model binary, fallback only when binary compatible or with known quality regression tolerance.
anika: Agreed. If fallback uses quantized variant, we should annotate the request trace with model_variant and run quick eval on a small prompt set during canary. auto-rollback on regression.
ben: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with the operator API, eviction_score formula, and warm/canary flow. want reviews from infra and evals teams.
maria: tagging @evals and @infra in the RFC when ready. thanks all. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks — let's keep operator changes minimal and implement opt-in staged fallback for a few pilot tenants first.
